newsitem.title: BOSNIA: World Bank, Bosnia said to agree on debt payment.
newsitem.headline: World Bank, Bosnia said to agree on debt payment.

text.p: Bosnia has reached an agreement with the World Bank on servicing of the country's debt after the government failed to pay an $8 million instalment on time, a World Bank official said on Tuesday.

"I want to give you the good news that we have an agreement with the government now, reached yesterday, on how to pay and service the debt," Caio Koch-Weser, managing director of World Bank operations, told reporters.
"We expect the payment almost immediately. The payment is assured," he said.
Bosnia inherited a $2 billion share of former Yugoslavia's debt and is currently servicing a consolidated $680 million loan to the World Bank with regular six-month payments.

The country failed to make an $8 million payment within a 30-day grace period which expired last Friday. Officials from the country's Serb entity had said they lacked funds to cover their $3.8 million share of the instalment.
World Bank officials did not say how the debt payment was resolved, calling it "an internal matter" between the country's Serb republic and Moslem-Croat federation.

Haris Silajdzic, the Moslem co-chairman of the central cabinet, indicated on Monday evening that the federation was ready to lend money to the Serb entity if the international community guaranteed repayment.
Silajdzic told state television that "money will be lent to that (Serb) entity and returned directly by the World Bank".
The government's official default on the debt service had prompted the World Bank to suspend approvals for loans and new reconstruction projects for Bosnia.

Monday's agreement brought Bosnia back into compliance and the World Bank would not have to resort to other penalties at its disposal, including suspending disbursements for ongoing projects after 60 days of non-payment.
Resolving the debt payment to the World Bank also removed one obstacle to clinching a $100 million deal with the International Monetary Fund.

But the Bosnian central parliament still has to adopt a package of economic reforms, including a law harmonising customs between Serb and Moslem-Croat territories, to meet preconditions for the IMF agreement.
Major powers have also demanded adoption of the economic legislation as a prerequisite for an international fund-raising conference for reconstruction aid scheduled for June 24 in Brussels.
